description: First-visit AGM tips — rendered once per screen via isFirstVisit(). Sprint 43.

/.title: Start the week here
/.body: Open Action Center first for injuries, owner requests, decisions, and next opponent. Before Advance Week, choose Roster, Depth Chart, Game Plan, or Inbox; unresolved items lock into the next game.

/roster.title: Find roles and uncovered backups
/roster.body: Sort by overall, age, or contract status. Decide who to protect, trade, cut, or replace before injuries expose uncovered backup jobs.

/depth-chart.title: Set starters and backups
/depth-chart.body: Order starters and first backups by role. Injuries and fatigue follow this saved order, so fix backup spots that would play after one injury before Advance Week.

/schedule.title: Set rest and weather calls
/schedule.body: Open Schedule for opponent strength, byes, short weeks, wind, and rain. Set rest or Game Plan calls before Advance Week; missed rest creates starter fatigue and weather shrinks calls.

/standings.title: Choose buy/sell timing
/standings.body: Open the division first and conference second before selling picks or resting starters. A missed tiebreaker turns one saved pick or rested starter into a lost playoff spot.

/inbox.title: Clear deadlines first
/inbox.body: Answer expiring decisions, press prompts, and front-office memos before Advance Week. Unanswered items expire, remove offers, or cut owner patience.

/game-plan.title: Protect healthy starters
/game-plan.body: Set calls from healthy starters, opponent pass rush, coverage, and run-defense targets. Ignoring injury flags exposes unavailable players, missed protections, or uncovered receivers.

/contracts.title: Cap space decides options
/contracts.body: Preview cap space and dead money before cuts, trades, extensions, or restructures. Restructure when the saved cap space solves a starter, backup, or injury job; otherwise future injury replacement and extension options shrink.

/trades.title: Name cost before trading
/trades.body: Name the return, cap hit, depth loss, and pick cost before accepting. Ignoring cap or depth weakens the lineup or blocks the next contract.

/scouting.title: Scout starter jobs
/scouting.body: Spend scouting budget on positions that must start soon. Unassigned role answers, medical limits, or coachability warnings force a draft reach or expensive free-agent patch.

/draft.title: Name role before pick
/draft.body: Name the top player on your board, the starter or backup job, and the rookie role before each pick. Reaching for quarterback or a starter job without a backup plan leaves a stronger pick unused and extends the roster gap.

/free-agency.title: Pay for roles
/free-agency.body: Name the role before bidding. Free agents cost more than draft picks, so a contract without a starter, backup, or injury role blocks cap space for extensions or trade fixes.

/training-camp.title: Set roles before cuts
/training-camp.body: Assign camp reps to lock roles before cuts and depth changes. Roleless reps lower morale, hide which player reaches the injury report first, and weaken depth all season.

/briefing.title: One screen, one week
/briefing.body: Open the AGM flags before Advance Week. Missing the briefing leaves injuries, tight cap space, or matchup fixes unresolved when the game locks.

/broadcast.title: Name result cause
/broadcast.body: Open Broadcast after games to name turnovers, sacks, injuries, and failed drives. Then change Roster, Depth Chart, or Game Plan before Advance Week; unfixed misses repeat next game.

/franchise.title: Open long-term after weekly lineup and cap
/franchise.body: Open Franchise after roster, cap, Game Plan, and injury choices to view owner approval, dynasty phase, and rule changes. This page will not fix next week's lineup, cap space, or injuries.
